chapter_note: Remarkably pure substrate chapter. Teaching purity 1.000 with zero editorial fatigue. The entire chapter follows a single systematic pattern — "Before X was discharged/born/rebelled, a place was prepared for it" — iterating through cosmic entities and their pre-prepared containment places. Both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic-architectural system: vessels→ditches, sea giant→great sea, waste→gehennas, rebels→hostels, abortions→gathering-place, watchers→prison, giants' children→cities. No editorial bridge, institutional, or exhortation vocabulary detected anywhere. This chapter appears to preserve a nearly intact substrate teaching sequence about cosmic foreknowledge and containment architecture. The enumeration structure (each paragraph = one cosmic entity and its prepared place) is characteristic of the oldest systematic teaching layer.

paragraphs.core_text: Understand also this other (matter): Before these vessels were discharged and swept down from heaven, first three ditches were fashioned and constructed for them, in which they would be bound and fettered.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opening transition 'Understand also this other (matter):' is a pedagogical marker within the teaching tradition, not a dialogue frame attribution. No honorifics, no Mani attribution, no 'once again' formula. The imperative voice ('understand') belongs to systematic instruction. Initiates the systematic enumeration pattern: Before X → Y was prepared.

paragraphs.core_text: Before the sea giant was discharged from the sphere, the Father of Life constructed a place for [him i]n this great sea that is within the walls, whereon the ships sail, and where the fullness shall [ ... ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure cosmic-architectural mapping: sea giant (cosmic entity) → great sea within the walls (cosmic geography). 'The sphere', 'the walls', 'the ships' are cosmic-architectural terms. High substrate score (17.5). The lacuna at end likely continued the cosmic description.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, before the [ ... ] was displayed to the worlds [ ... ] the earth [ ... ... f]ell to the sea and its thought shaped it, the Father of Life constructed a place for it in [the ... ... ] below the four mountains, above the mountains of the heavens above [ ... ] that [ ... ] a great plain it digs in Matter in the midst of the worlds. When the Adamant of Light was sent to it, he hastened after it to that place, smote it and threw it between mountains in the place made ready for it [ ... ] is set fast upon it till the end of the universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Dense cosmic geography: four mountains, mountains of the heavens, great plain in Matter, midst of the worlds. The Adamant of Light is a cosmic agent performing a cosmic function — smiting and imprisoning a cosmic entity in a prepared cosmic place. Heavy lacunae but all recoverable content is systematic cosmic process description. Both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: Before the waste and dirt of Darkness were swept out from creation, gehennas were constructed in which the waste might be covered till the dissolution of the universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Concise iteration of the pattern: waste/dirt of Darkness (cosmic substance) → gehennas (cosmic containment). 'Gehennas' here functions as cosmic architecture, not moral/eschatological application. 'Dissolution of the universe' is cosmic temporal horizon. Capitalizing Darkness as it functions as a cosmic domain.

paragraphs.core_text: Before the rebels rose up, they whose corps rebelled in the ruling-power above and below, they [ ... ] outside, and also the tyrants in whose heart it lay [to ty]rannise amongst the murk and the clouds and winds and spirits and storms; for them were constructed in the great outer sea seven hostels, places whence they are thrown into the depths and the darkness [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic rebellion mapped to cosmic containment. 'Rebels', 'corps', 'ruling-power above and below', 'tyrants', 'murk', 'clouds and winds and spirits and storms' — all cosmic entities/phenomena. 'Seven hostels' in the 'great outer sea' — cosmic geography with numerical specificity characteristic of substrate enumeration. Both sides entirely within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, before the abortions [fell ... ...] to the earth, there was set apart [ ... ]: they are gathered in and dwell therein.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Brief iteration — 'abortions' are cosmic entities (demonic offspring) in Manichaean cosmology, not human abortions. Their prepared place is lost in lacuna. The pattern 'Before X... a place was set apart' continues the systematic enumeration.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, before the watchers rebelled and came down from heaven, a prison was fashioned and constructed for them in the depths of the earth, below the mountains.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Watchers tradition (Enochic) integrated into the cosmic containment schema. 'Again' is an enumeration marker continuing the list. Watchers (cosmic beings) → prison in the depths of the earth below the mountains (cosmic geography). Both sides stay within the cosmic system. The Watcher tradition itself may be very old substrate shared with Enochic literature.

paragraphs.core_text: Before the children of the giants were born, they who had [no] knowledge of righteousness in them nor divinity, thirty-six cities were assigned and constructed for them wherein the children of [the giants would] live; they who would come to beget from each other, they who shall spend ten hundred years alive.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Final iteration: giants' children (cosmic beings) → thirty-six cities (cosmic geography). 'Thirty-six' is precise numerical specification characteristic of substrate systematization. 'Ten hundred years' is cosmic temporal measure. 'Knowledge of righteousness... nor divinity' describes what these beings ARE within the cosmic system — not moral exhortation. The enumeration pattern closes here, completing the catalogue of prepared containments.
